measure: a share of a total, computed against a window or subtotal
gold_sql:
WITH source_peptide_avg AS (
    SELECT
        apm.measurement_source_id,
        apm.peptide_id,
        AVG(apm.measurement_value) AS avg_measurement_value
    FROM allele_peptide_measurements AS apm
    WHERE apm.measurement_value IS NOT NULL
      AND apm.peptide_id IS NOT NULL
      AND apm.measurement_source_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY apm.measurement_source_id, apm.peptide_id
),
eligible_pairs AS (
    SELECT
        spa.measurement_source_id,
        spa.peptide_id,
        spa.avg_measurement_value
    FROM source_peptide_avg AS spa
    JOIN peptides AS p
      ON p.peptide_id = spa.peptide_id
    WHERE spa.avg_measurement_value >
          (
              SELECT AVG(spa2.avg_measurement_value)
              FROM source_peptide_avg AS spa2
              WHERE spa2.measurement_source_id = spa.measurement_source_id
          )
),
ranked_pairs AS (
    SELECT
        ep.measurement_source_id,
        ep.peptide_id,
        ep.avg_measurement_value,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY ep.measurement_source_id
            ORDER BY ep.avg_measurement_value DESC, ep.peptide_id
        ) AS peptide_rank
    FROM eligible_pairs AS ep
),
survivors AS (
    SELECT
        rp.measurement_source_id,
        rp.peptide_id,
        rp.avg_measurement_value
    FROM ranked_pairs AS rp
    WHERE rp.peptide_rank <= 2
),
source_survivor_totals AS (
    SELECT
        s.measurement_source_id,
        ms.source_description AS source_description,
        SUM(s.avg_measurement_value) AS survivor_total_value
    FROM survivors AS s
    JOIN measurement_sources AS ms
      ON ms.source_id = s.measurement_source_id
    GROUP BY s.measurement_source_id, ms.source_description
)
SELECT
    measurement_source_id AS measurement_source_id,
    source_description AS source_description,
    survivor_total_value AS survivor_total_value,
    ROUND(
        1.0 * survivor_total_value / SUM(survivor_total_value) OVER (),
        6
    ) AS survivor_value_share_of_total
FROM source_survivor_totals
ORDER BY survivor_value_share_of_total DESC, measurement_source_id

measure: a label assigned by thresholds on a computed quantity
gold_sql:
WITH output_step_metadata AS (
    SELECT
        dps.output_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT dps.step_id) AS active_step_count,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN om.is_active = 1 THEN om.metadata_id END) AS active_metadata_count
    FROM data_processing_steps AS dps
    JOIN digital_outputs AS do
        ON do.output_id = dps.output_id
    LEFT JOIN output_metadata AS om
        ON om.output_id = do.output_id
    WHERE dps.is_active = 1
      AND do.is_public = 1
    GROUP BY dps.output_id
),
qualified_outputs AS (
    SELECT
        output_id,
        active_step_count,
        active_metadata_count,
        CAST(active_metadata_count AS REAL) / NULLIF(active_step_count, 0) AS metadata_per_step_ratio
    FROM output_step_metadata
    WHERE active_step_count >= 2
)
SELECT
    CASE
        WHEN AVG(metadata_per_step_ratio) >= 5 THEN 'very_high_metadata_density'
        WHEN AVG(metadata_per_step_ratio) >= 3 THEN 'high_metadata_density'
        WHEN AVG(metadata_per_step_ratio) >= 1.5 THEN 'moderate_metadata_density'
        ELSE 'low_metadata_density'
    END AS metadata_density_label
FROM qualified_outputs
question: Across all publicly accessible digital outputs that have at least two active processing steps, classify the overall metadata density based on the average number of active metadata entries per active processing step. Return only the resulting metadata-density label, where the average ratio is labeled as very_high_metadata_density if it is at least 5, high_metadata_density if at least 3, moderate_metadata_density if at least 1.5, and low_metadata_density otherwise.

gate.row_grain: A single overall metadata-density classification label for all eligible digital outputs combined.
gate.why: The question asks to calculate a single overall average ratio across all qualifying digital outputs and return only the corresponding classification label.

measure: a per-unit rate (per day, per member, per km)
gold_sql:
WITH article_access_stats AS (
    SELECT
        a.article_id,
        a.title AS article_title,
        a.status AS article_status,
        a.open_access_type,
        COUNT(al.access_id) AS total_accesses,
        COUNT(DISTINCT al.user_id) AS distinct_users,
        COUNT(DISTINCT al.access_date) AS active_days,
        AVG(CASE WHEN al.user_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1.0 ELSE NULL END) AS avg_user_presence,
        MIN(al.access_date) AS first_access_date,
        MAX(al.access_date) AS last_access_date,
        COUNT(DISTINCT al.access_type) AS distinct_access_types
    FROM articles AS a
    LEFT JOIN access_logs AS al
        ON a.article_id = al.article_id
    GROUP BY
        a.article_id,
        a.title,
        a.status,
        a.open_access_type
),
article_user_roles AS (
    SELECT
        al.article_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN u.role IS NOT NULL THEN u.role END) AS distinct_user_roles,
        CASE
            WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN u.role IS NOT NULL THEN u.role END) = 0 THEN 'no_known_roles'
            WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN u.role IS NOT NULL THEN u.role END) = 1 THEN 'single_role'
            ELSE 'multi_role'
        END AS user_role_mix_label
    FROM access_logs AS al
    LEFT JOIN users AS u
        ON al.user_id = u.user_id
    GROUP BY al.article_id
)
SELECT
    s.article_id,
    s.article_title,
    ROUND(
        COALESCE(
            1.0 * s.total_accesses / NULLIF(s.active_days, 0),
            0
        ),
        2
    ) AS accesses_per_active_day,
    s.total_accesses AS total_access_count,
    s.distinct_users AS distinct_user_count,
    ROUND(
        COALESCE(
            1.0 * s.total_accesses / NULLIF(s.distinct_users, 0),
            0
        ),
        2
    ) AS accesses_per_user,
    ROUND(COALESCE(s.avg_user_presence, 0), 3) AS avg_non_null_user_indicator,
    s.distinct_access_types AS distinct_access_type_count,
    COALESCE(r.distinct_user_roles, 0) AS distinct_user_role_count,
    s.first_access_date AS first_access_date,
    s.last_access_date AS last_access_date,
    CASE
        WHEN s.total_accesses = 0 THEN 'no_access'
        WHEN s.active_days IS NULL OR s.active_days = 0 THEN 'undated_access'
        WHEN 1.0 * s.total_accesses / s.active_days >= 3 THEN 'high_daily_activity'
        WHEN 1.0 * s.total_accesses / s.active_days >= 1 THEN 'moderate_daily_activity'
        ELSE 'low_daily_activity'
    END AS activity_rate_label,
    COALESCE(r.user_role_mix_label, 'no_known_roles') AS user_role_mix_label,
    s.article_status,
    s.open_access_type
FROM article_access_stats AS s
LEFT JOIN article_user_roles AS r
    ON s.article_id = r.article_id
WHERE s.total_accesses > 0
ORDER BY accesses_per_active_day DESC, s.total_accesses DESC, s.article_id
question: For every article that has at least one recorded access event, list the article ID, article title, accesses per active day, total access count, distinct user count, accesses per user, the average non-null user indicator across access events, distinct access type count, distinct user role count, first access date, last access date, an activity-rate label, the user-role-mix label, article status, and open access type. Define accesses per active day as total accesses divided by the number of different access dates for that article, accesses per user as total accesses divided by the number of different users who accessed it, classify activity as no access, undated access, high daily activity for at least 3 accesses per active day, moderate daily activity for at least 1 but less than 3, and low daily activity otherwise, and classify the user-role mix as no known roles, single role, or multi role based on how many different known user roles appear among the accessing users; order the results by accesses per active day from highest to lowest, then by total accesses from highest to lowest, and then by article ID.

gate.row_grain: One row per article that has at least one recorded access event
columns: Average non-null user indicator across access events
gate.why: The question specifies explicit definitions, column outputs, filtering criteria, and ordering rules for articles with access events.

measure: a label assigned by thresholds on a computed quantity
naive_sql:
SELECT
    r.reviewer_id AS reviewer_id,
    COALESCE(r.first_name, '') || CASE WHEN r.first_name IS NOT NULL AND r.last_name IS NOT NULL THEN ' ' ELSE '' END || COALESCE(r.last_name, '') AS reviewer_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT rv.review_id) AS review_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT coi.conflict_id) AS conflict_count,
    CASE
        WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT rv.review_id) = 0 THEN 'no_reviews'
        WHEN 1.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT coi.conflict_id) / COUNT(DISTINCT rv.review_id) >= 2.0 THEN 'high_conflict_rate'
        WHEN 1.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT coi.conflict_id) / COUNT(DISTINCT rv.review_id) >= 1.0 THEN 'medium_conflict_rate'
        ELSE 'low_conflict_rate'
    END AS conflict_rate_label
FROM reviewers AS r
JOIN reviews AS rv
    ON r.reviewer_id = rv.reviewer_id
LEFT JOIN conflicts_of_interest AS coi
    ON r.reviewer_id = coi.reviewer_id
GROUP BY
    r.reviewer_id,
    r.first_name,
    r.last_name
ORDER BY r.reviewer_id
gold_sql:
WITH reviewer_review_counts AS (
    SELECT
        r.reviewer_id AS reviewer_id,
        COUNT(rv.review_id) AS review_count
    FROM reviewers AS r
    LEFT JOIN reviews AS rv
        ON r.reviewer_id = rv.reviewer_id
    GROUP BY r.reviewer_id
),
reviewer_conflict_counts AS (
    SELECT
        r.reviewer_id AS reviewer_id,
        COUNT(coi.conflict_id) AS conflict_count
    FROM reviewers AS r
    LEFT JOIN conflicts_of_interest AS coi
        ON r.reviewer_id = coi.reviewer_id
    GROUP BY r.reviewer_id
)
SELECT
    r.reviewer_id AS reviewer_id,
    COALESCE(r.first_name, '') || CASE WHEN r.first_name IS NOT NULL AND r.last_name IS NOT NULL THEN ' ' ELSE '' END || COALESCE(r.last_name, '') AS reviewer_name,
    rrc.review_count AS review_count,
    rcc.conflict_count AS conflict_count,
    CASE
        WHEN rrc.review_count = 0 THEN 'no_reviews'
        WHEN 1.0 * rcc.conflict_count / rrc.review_count >= 2.0 THEN 'high_conflict_rate'
        WHEN 1.0 * rcc.conflict_count / rrc.review_count >= 1.0 THEN 'medium_conflict_rate'
        ELSE 'low_conflict_rate'
    END AS conflict_rate_label
FROM reviewers AS r
LEFT JOIN reviewer_review_counts AS rrc
    ON r.reviewer_id = rrc.reviewer_id
LEFT JOIN reviewer_conflict_counts AS rcc
    ON r.reviewer_id = rcc.reviewer_id
ORDER BY r.reviewer_id

measure: a count of events per entity
gold_sql:
WITH presentation_counts AS (
    SELECT
        project_id,
        COUNT(*) AS presentation_count
    FROM presentations
    WHERE project_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY project_id
),
publication_counts AS (
    SELECT
        project_id,
        COUNT(*) AS publication_count
    FROM publications
    WHERE project_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY project_id
)
SELECT
    fp.project_id AS project_id,
    COALESCE(pc.presentation_count, 0) AS presentation_count,
    COALESCE(puc.publication_count, 0) AS publication_count
FROM funded_projects AS fp
LEFT JOIN presentation_counts AS pc
    ON fp.project_id = pc.project_id
LEFT JOIN publication_counts AS puc
    ON fp.project_id = puc.project_id
WHERE COALESCE(pc.presentation_count, 0) > 0
   OR COALESCE(puc.publication_count, 0) > 0
ORDER BY presentation_count DESC, publication_count DESC, fp.project_id
question: For each funded project, can you report the project’s identifier, the total number of presentations linked to that project, and the total number of publications linked to that project? Only include projects that have at least one presentation or at least one publication, and sort the results by presentation count in descending order, then by publication count in descending order, and finally by project identifier.

gate.row_grain: A funded project that has at least one presentation or at least one publication
columns: total number of presentations linked to the project
total number of publications linked to the project
gate.why: The question clearly specifies the required fields, aggregate metrics, filtering condition, and multi-level sorting criteria without ambiguity.

measure: a label assigned by thresholds on a computed quantity
gold_sql:
WITH country_access_stats AS (
    SELECT
        c.country_id,
        c.country_name,
        COUNT(ua.access_id) AS total_access_events,
        COUNT(DISTINCT i.individual_id) AS total_individuals_in_country,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN ua.access_id IS NOT NULL THEN i.individual_id END) AS accessed_individuals
    FROM countries AS c
    JOIN individuals AS i
        ON i.native_country_id = c.country_id
    LEFT JOIN user_access AS ua
        ON ua.individual_id = i.individual_id
    GROUP BY
        c.country_id,
        c.country_name
),
country_rates AS (
    SELECT
        country_id,
        country_name,
        total_access_events,
        total_individuals_in_country,
        accessed_individuals,
        CAST(total_access_events AS REAL) / NULLIF(total_individuals_in_country, 0) AS access_events_per_individual,
        CAST(accessed_individuals AS REAL) / NULLIF(total_individuals_in_country, 0) AS accessed_individual_rate
    FROM country_access_stats
)
SELECT
    country_name AS country_name,
    total_access_events AS total_access_events,
    total_individuals_in_country AS total_individuals_in_country,
    accessed_individuals AS accessed_individuals,
    ROUND(access_events_per_individual, 2) AS access_events_per_individual,
    ROUND(accessed_individual_rate, 2) AS accessed_individual_rate,
    CASE
        WHEN access_events_per_individual >= 100 THEN 'very_high_access_intensity'
        WHEN access_events_per_individual >= 25 THEN 'high_access_intensity'
        WHEN access_events_per_individual >= 5 THEN 'medium_access_intensity'
        ELSE 'low_access_intensity'
    END AS access_intensity_label
FROM country_rates
WHERE total_individuals_in_country > 0
ORDER BY
    access_events_per_individual DESC,
    country_name
